prompt:
High-fidelity desktop web UI design comp, landscape, for the organizer dashboard of a retreat-planning survey product. This is a designed interface screen, not a poster: it must read as a screenshot of a working admin product.

Layout scaffold, a fixed left command rail plus a wide content area, on a solid warm near-black background (#0b0908, no photograph). Left rail, about one quarter of the width, separated from the content by a single vertical 1px white hairline: at top a stacked two-line ultra-condensed tall white grotesque title "ATMOSPHERIC / ORGANIZER." in capitals; beneath it a vertical stack of large white numerals with small tracked uppercase labels — "37 RESPONSES", "24 YES", "9 MAYBE", "11 NEED TRAVEL HELP" — each separated by thin hairlines; then a small "LOCATIONS" ranked ledger of five rows (Palm Springs 41, Joshua Tree 33, San Diego 28, Coachella Valley 19, LA metro 12) with thin white tally bars; then two toggle rows "REOPEN SURVEY" and "LATE PASSES · 2" with small round toggle knobs; at the rail bottom a fully rounded white pill button with black text "Export CSV". Right content area: top half is a calendar availability heatmap under a small condensed header "WHEN CAN THEY COME" and a quiet subline "Sept 1 – Nov 15"; three month grids side by side labeled SEPTEMBER, OCTOBER, NOVEMBER; each day a small rounded square filled white at opacity proportional to availability, bright equals many available, faint equals few, faint day numerals inside, several edge cells split horizontally into a bright top half and faint bottom half; directly under it one highlighted hairline row "BEST WINDOW · THU OCT 8 – SUN OCT 11 · 29 OF 33". Bottom half of the content area: a wide responses table of thin hairline-separated rows, each with a small circular avatar, handle like @maren.dev, name, city, interest word (YES/MAYBE/NO), travel answer, range count, and an updated date; column headers in small tracked uppercase. Table cut off at the page bottom implying scroll.

Every interface element is pure white at varying opacity on the near-black ground; no second UI color, no cards, no boxes, no shadows; thin 1px hairline rules structure everything; subtle film grain overall; flat matte finish, no gloss, no 3D. No browser chrome.
